CHAPTER 44 
Rama slays Maricha 
HAVING issued this command to his brother, that invincible 
warrior, the Delight of the House of Raghu, endowed with 
great prowess, girded on his sword in its golden scabbard, and 
taking up his triply-curved bow, his personal insignia and two 
quivers filled with arrows, he set forth with long strides. 
Beholding that lndra among Men, the king of the beasts in 
fear disappeared only to re-appear once more. 
Girt with his sword and bearing his bow in his hand, Rama 
ran in the direction of the deer and beheld it in all its beauty, 
close to him. Bow in hand, fixing his eyes on the fawn as it 
fled into the forest, he saw it sometimes taking a single bnund, 
and then, in order to lure him on, allowing him to draw closer. 
Timid and fearful, it would leap into the air, at times becoming 
visible and then disappearing in the depths of the thickets. 
As in the autumn, stray clouds pass across the moon's face, 
so that she sometimes shines in all her brilliance and at others

brief.summary_1line: Rama pursues and kills the demon Maricha disguised as a golden deer, who dies crying out in Rama’s voice to lure Lakshmana away.

image_candidates.scene_text: Rama draws a blazing arrow and releases it as the golden deer leaps through the forest clearing.
The arrow strikes the deer mid‑leap, and the creature transforms into the huge demon Maricha, bloodied and collapsing to the earth.
Dying Maricha in demon form cries out 'O Sita, O Lakshmana!' in Rama’s voice while lying wounded in the forest.

deep.rich_summary: Rama leaves the hermitage to pursue the dazzling golden deer that has enchanted Sita, instructing Lakshmana to remain behind and guard her carefully with the help of the wise vulture Jatayu. The deer—actually the demon Maricha in disguise—repeatedly appears and vanishes, luring Rama deeper into the forest through illusion and cunning. Finally, realizing the deception, Rama unleashes a blazing, divinely fashioned arrow that strikes Maricha. Mortally wounded, the demon abandons the deer form and, recalling Ravana’s scheme, imitates Rama’s voice and cries out to Sita and Lakshmana. Rama immediately understands the danger: the cry may draw Lakshmana away and leave Sita alone. This moment is pivotal, as Maricha’s dying trick triggers the chain of events leading directly to Sita’s abduction.

highlight_spans.why: Rama’s opening resolve and instruction establish duty, protection of Sita, and the moral seriousness with which he approaches the hunt.
The commitment to slay or capture the mysterious deer foreshadows the trap that will separate Rama from Sita.
The tension builds as Rama pursues the elusive deer, emphasizing illusion and the fatal deception orchestrated by Maricha.

top_scenes.scene_text: Rama, bow drawn and sword at his side, strides through the forest chasing the radiant golden deer that flickers in and out among the trees.
Rama releases a blazing divine arrow like a fiery serpent that strikes the deer mid‑leap, revealing the demon Maricha as he crashes to the earth.
The dying Maricha transforms back into a gigantic blood‑covered titan and cries out in Rama’s voice, calling ‘O Sita, O Lakshmana!’ across the forest.
